The manner in which Y+(!) changes with noise is reminiscent of coherence resonance in excitable systems [23].

The effect is well known for classical systems 164-108], but has appeared only relatively recently in quantum systems [121, 169]. A notable difference between our results in Fig, 8 and coherence resonance is that we have not operated the noise-free quantum Fitzhugh-Nagumo system in the excitable regime (defined classically by having a stable fixed point in the system while being close to the supercritical Hopf bifurcation).
